Source ecc8b4db4896dd08 preamble and §1 give the paired quantity, affine invariance and continuity, and §4 (R), (6) supplies the global compactness argument. Source 3787afd8b1ed0167 §1, (2)–(4) gives the inscribed-simplex normalization. Both archived digests match. The frozen proof's box formulation yields the same class because s(C)=|T| also bounds all the barycentric coordinates by vertex replacement.

An attaining inscribed d-simplex exists by determinant continuity on compact vertex tuples, and it has positive volume. After affine transport, T is an inscribed maximizer. Replacing any one vertex bounds |λ_i(x)| by one, hence all ambient coordinates lie in the common box. Conversely s(C)=|T| in the displayed class makes T a maximizer. The two inclusions and s(C)=|T| are closed, so Blaschke compactness applies. Every limit contains T, ruling out degeneration.

If a normalized member C is a simplex, then |C|=s(C)=|T|. Because T⊆C, any point of C outside T would form a positive-volume cone beyond a facet and contradict the volume identity. Thus T is the only simplex in the normalized class.

The rigidity theorem uses the same functional: dividing u by its norm and rescaling |s| only relabels the pair. Normalized uniform measures converge in total variation in the compact class by indicator convergence off the null boundary in the fixed box and volumes at least |T|. Each averaged probability changes by at most one total-variation distance. This bound passes through minima and suprema on common domains. For each ambient point outside its body a strictly separating shift-zero cap has zero mass, so the ambient supremum agrees with the attained maximum on the body.

The class d_{H,∞}(C,T)≥ε_d is closed in the compact normalized class, and ε_d>0 by the local construction. Its continuous minimum is positive when nonempty, since a zero would force C=T. The empty-class convention β_d=1 is harmless because then no far case occurs.

For distance ≤ε_d the frozen relative theorem applies in the normalized frame to every minimizing enclosure and yields coefficient 4/(Γc). For distance >ε_d the body belongs to the far class, so 1−|K|/|S|≤1≤(P(K)−Γ)/β_d. The shared boundary is covered, and max of the two coefficients suffices. An invertible affine map preserves the paired depth and transforms all enclosing volumes by the same positive factor, so it bijects the minimizing enclosures.
